pr_md.text:
# Audit and remediation: orders-service

Audits `src/` against the behavior contract in `README.md` and fixes what it
found: two access-control defects, three correctness defects, one dead
function, one speculative abstraction, and one layering violation. `README.md`
is unchanged — it was the oracle, and the code now matches it.

Base: `c57a98b`. Nothing is committed, pushed, or opened as a pull request.

## What changed

### Security

**A customer could read any other customer's order.**
`GET /orders/:id` called `orders.get(params.id)`, which takes no actor, so the
ownership check in `getOwned` never ran — `README.md` says customers read only
their own orders and that a resource the caller may not see returns 404. The
route now calls `orders.getOwned(user, params.id)`. To stop the same mistake
being made again, `get` is no longer on the order service's public surface:
`src/orders/service.js` exposes no order read that does not name an actor, so a
route cannot fetch an order unscoped. `ship`, `deliver`, and `markPaid` still
use it internally and are already `requireAdmin`.

**`GET /reports/:name` served any file the process could read.**
The route joined the caller-supplied name straight onto `REPORT_DIR`. The
router decodes each path segment after splitting, so `%2F` survived as one
segment and decoded to a separator: `GET /reports/..%2Fsecret.txt` returned a
file above the export directory. Admin-only, but `README.md` scopes the route
to exports in `REPORT_DIR`, and an export name is not a filesystem path. The
download route now accepts only names this service generates
(`/^orders-\d+-[0-9a-f]{6}\.csv$/`), which no separator, traversal segment, or
null byte can match, and the generator sits next to the pattern in the same
module so the two cannot drift unnoticed.

**Token signature comparison is now constant-time** (`src/auth/tokens.js`).
`signature !== sign(payload)` short-circuits on the first differing byte;
`crypto.timingSafeEqual` behind a length check does not. This is hardening, not
a demonstrated exploit — no test can observe a timing side channel, so it is
verified by review only.

### Correctness

**`totalPages` undercounted every partial page** (`src/lib/pagination.js`).
`Math.floor(items.length / pageSize)` reports 1 page for 25 items at 20 per
page, so a client paging until `page === totalPages` silently never sees the
last page. `README.md` defines `totalPages` as the pages needed to show every
item, at least 1 — that is `Math.ceil`. It affects `GET /orders` and
`GET /users`, the only paginated endpoints.

**A shipped order could be cancelled** (`src/orders/service.js`).
`TRANSITIONS.shipped` listed `cancelled`, contradicting `README.md`: a shipped
or delivered order can no longer be cancelled. A customer could cancel an order
already in transit, after payment. `shipped` now allows only `delivered`.

**Order totals were not exact to the cent** (`src/lib/money.js`).
`sumLines` summed `unitPrice * quantity` in floating point, so three items at
`0.1` stored and returned `total: 0.30000000000000004`, and seven at `8.6`
returned `60.199999999999996`. `README.md` requires an order total exact to the
cent. Totals are now summed in integer cents and converted once
(`itemsTotalCents` / `fromCents`). The CSV export hid this behind `toFixed(2)`;
the JSON API did not.

### Dead code and simplification

**`parseCookies` deleted** (`src/http/respond.js`). No caller anywhere in `src`
or `test`; authentication is `Authorization: Bearer` only, and the package is
private with no external consumers.

**The payment provider registry collapsed into one function.**
`src/payments/providers.js` held a module-level `Map`, a `registerProvider`
validator, and a name lookup to serve exactly one provider. Nothing ever
registered a second one, nothing ever set `options.paymentProvider`, and
`README.md` mentions no provider choice — a plugin seam with one plug and no
named second instance. It is now `src/payments/gateway.js` exporting `charge`,
which is what the file actually contains. `createPaymentService` no longer
takes a `provider` name.

**The order-total rule now has one authoritative implementation.**
`payments/service.js` carried its own `orderTotalCents` loop, a second copy of
the rule `orders/service.js` applies when it stores a total. Two copies of one
money rule can disagree; both now go through `src/lib/money.js`.

**The users route no longer reaches past its service into the data store.**
`registerUserRoutes` received the `store` and ran
`store.list('users').map(users.toPublic)` — the only route module that touched
storage, and the only reason `toPublic` was on the service's public surface. It
now calls `users.list(query)`, matching how `GET /orders` already works.
`src/users/service.js` owns the query and the pagination; `toPublic` is
internal again.

## Evidence

Every command was run from the repository root on Node 24 (`engines` asks for
`>=20`).

| Command | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `node --test` (before any change) | `pass 20  fail 0` — baseline |
| `node --test` (after) | `pass 29  fail 0`, ~1.1 s |
| `node --test test/pagination.test.js` | `pass 3  fail 0` |
| `node --test test/architecture.test.js` | `pass 1  fail 0` |
| `APP_SECRET=… ADMIN_EMAIL=… ADMIN_PASSWORD=… node src/app.js` | boots, logs `orders-service listening on 3457`; `GET /users/me` → 401, `POST /sessions` → 201 with a token |

All 20 pre-existing tests still pass, unmodified.

### Each defect, reproduced before and after

Driven by a probe script outside the repository against the real HTTP server,
so the router, the guard, and the services are all in the path.

| Probe | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Bob reads Alice's order: `GET /orders/<alice-order>` | `200` with Alice's full order, including her `userId` | `404 {"error":"order not found"}` |
| `GET /reports/..%2Fprobe-secret.txt` as admin | `200 "TOP-SECRET"` — a file outside `REPORT_DIR` | `404 {"error":"report not found"}` |
| `paginate(25 items, pageSize 20).totalPages` | `1` | `2` |
| Cancel a shipped order | `200`, status `cancelled` | `409 order cannot move from shipped to cancelled` |
| Order of 3 × `0.1`, via the JSON API | `total: 0.30000000000000004` | `total: 0.3` |
| Order of 7 × `8.6`, via the JSON API | `total: 60.199999999999996` | `total: 60.2` |

### Tests added

Placed at the earliest stage that can observe each failure. The two
authorization defects exist only once the router, guard, and service are wired
together, so they are tested over HTTP; `totalPages` is pure, so it is tested
directly.

- `test/pagination.test.js` (new, pure unit) — `totalPages` across
  0/1/20/21/25/40/41 items and a non-default `pageSize`, page slicing,
  `pageSize` capped at 100, and fallbacks for unusable values.
- `test/orders.test.js` — a customer reading another customer's order gets 404;
  a shipped and then a delivered order cannot be cancelled; order totals are
  exact to the cent for `0.1×3`, `8.6×7`, `1.15×3`, and a mixed-line order, each
  followed by a payment of that exact total.
- `test/reports.test.js` — six download names that are not exports of this
  service (encoded forward and back slashes, an absolute path, a null byte, a
  `.bak` suffix) all return 404 and never leak a file planted outside
  `REPORT_DIR`; and three freshly generated export names are all accepted by the
  download route, so the generator and the allowlist cannot drift apart.
- `test/architecture.test.js` (new) — the layering rule the users fix restored,
  as an executable check rather than prose: no module outside the composition
  root imports the data store, and no route module works with a `store` at all.
  Confirmed non-hollow by reintroducing the violation, which fails the test with
  `users/routes.js works with the data store instead of a service`, then
  reverting.

### Structural effect

Measured on the static require graph, before → after:

- Subsystem-count (files in `src/`): 17 → 17 (unchanged)
- Dependency-edges (internal requires): 25 → 25 — `users/routes → lib/pagination`
  moved to `users/service → lib/pagination`
- Max-chain-depth: 3 hops → 3 hops (unchanged)
- Static cycle: Pass → Pass
- Subsystem-kinds: 8 → 7 — the module-level mutable registry is gone, and no
  sibling used that shape

The edge the change actually removes is not an import: `users/routes` received
the store by injection from `src/app.js`, a route-to-storage edge that skipped
the service layer. Import-graph counts cannot see it, which is why
`test/architecture.test.js` checks the wiring too.

## What I did not verify

- **Timing-channel resistance of the token compare.** No test observes it;
  `crypto.timingSafeEqual` is accepted on review. The length pre-check leaks
  signature length, which is fixed at 43 characters for a genuine token.
- **Concurrency.** The in-memory store is single-process and the service does no
  `await` between reading an order's state and writing it, so no interleaving
  was tested. This stops being true if the store is ever replaced by anything
  with real I/O: `payments.capture` → `orders.markPaid` would then be a
  read-modify-write race that permits double payment. Not changed here; it is
  not a defect in the current single-process design.
- **Rate limiting on `POST /sessions`.** Password verification is `scryptSync`
  with no attempt throttling, so the endpoint is both brute-forceable and a CPU
  denial-of-service surface. `README.md` states no requirement here, so I left it
  alone rather than invent a threshold. Run
  `grep -rn "scryptSync\|/sessions" src/` to see the surface.
- **CSV injection in the export.** `toCsvRow` writes UUIDs, a status from a fixed
  set, a number, and an ISO timestamp, so no field is user-controlled today. It
  is unquoted and unescaped, so that holds only as long as that stays true —
  adding, say, a customer name to the export would reopen it.
- **The Stage 2/5 detection gap for the layering rule.** A forbidden
  architectural dependency is catchable in the editor or at build time; this repo
  has no linter and declares no third-party dependencies, so the rule is enforced
  at the test stage instead. Closing the gap properly means
  `npm i -D eslint eslint-plugin-boundaries` and an architecture config — a
  dependency decision for the owner, not an audit change.
- **Token revocation and `APP_SECRET` rotation.** Tokens are stateless and valid
  for their full hour; nothing invalidates one early. Out of scope and unchanged.
- **Performance.** No benchmark was run; nothing here is on a measured hot path.
